meta.title: Questions, knowns and unknowns — what must be answered before a decision is reasonable
meta.rule: Every row separates what we KNOW (with its source) from what we DO NOT KNOW. A question is only 'answerable now' if a named process can produce the answer from a source we can reach. Questions whose answer needs data that does not exist in this repository are marked blocked and given the acquisition step and its cost.
meta.sort: blocking_decisions desc, then status order: open-blocking, open, answerable

legend.answerable: can be answered from committed data or a reachable official source, without new data acquisition
legend.open: answer requires a decision or external input that is not data (a rule, a policy, a licence)
legend.blocked: answer requires data or access we do not have; the acquisition step and cost are stated
legend.answered: answered; the answer and where it is recorded

questions.question: Does anything in this model beat the closing line?
questions.known: No. The incremental-information coefficient is -0.019 (p = 0.881) after controlling for the close; the model's spread MAE is 10.39 against the market's 10.25 on the same games.
questions.unknown: Whether the model adds information in any subset (bucket) even if it loses pooled. Not yet tested by bucket.
questions.how_to_answer: Bucket the residual analysis by favourite size, rest, roof and division, with a Benjamini-Hochberg correction across buckets. Committed predictions.csv already carries model_margin, market_margin and result.
questions.verified_by: decision-hub/scripts/audit_root.py re-derives the pooled numbers from data/derived/games.csv.gz

questions.question: Is the ATS market exploitable by simple public angles?
questions.known: Under the published pooled test, 'no', but that test is an arithmetic identity (FL-DH-01). Under the one-sided test, the home cover rate is 48.91% with a 95% CI of 47.73-50.09% on 6,892 games, two-sided p = 0.073. That is inconclusive, not zero.
questions.unknown: Whether a specific angle is exploitable. 12 classic angles were screened and none survived Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.10.
questions.how_to_answer: Keep the one-sided test; add a per-angle table with the one-sided CI and the corrected p, and publish the intervals next to the point estimates.
questions.verified_by: recomputed from committed data in decision-hub/data/root_audit.json

questions.question: Are same-game parlay legs correlated enough to change the price?
questions.known: Yes. QB passing yards vs WR1 receiving yards r = +0.562; the four-leg same-team joint probability is 11.1% against 5.7% under independence, so pricing the legs independently understates the joint by a factor of about two.
questions.unknown: The correlation's uncertainty, and whether the Gaussian copula parameter is stable across seasons. No interval is published.
questions.how_to_answer: Bootstrap the pairwise coefficients by season and by team, then propagate the interval into the SGP price.
questions.verified_by: the joint-vs-product figures are independently reproduced in the project's own verification record (sgp.* checks)

questions.question: What does a missing starter actually do to the line?
questions.known: Which players are reported Out/Doubtful each week and where they sit on their club's depth chart (this session's tracker: 636 absences with a rank in 2026).
questions.unknown: The effect size. Nothing in the repository measures how many points the market moves when a 1st-string player is ruled out, so no strategy can be sized from it.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare the closing line with the previous week's closing line for the same team, holding opponent strength roughly constant, and regress the move on the depth-weighted absence count. Needs a line that is timestamped (Q-05).
questions.verified_by: the depth ranks themselves are computed from the 2026 depth-chart snapshot; the effect is unmeasured

questions.question: Can a timestamped price be obtained, legally and reproducibly?
questions.known: No. The feed stores only the closing line and its odds. No opening line, no timestamp, no prop price. No sportsbook account, limit or jurisdiction is verified.
questions.unknown: Whether a licensed feed or an operator API is available to this project, at what cost, and under what terms of use. Scraping a sportsbook board would need a licence review before it could be relied on.
questions.how_to_answer: Two options: (a) log prices live, going forward, from a licensed source with written permission; (b) buy a historical odds vendor (not an official league source, so it would be a class-2 source on the sources page).
questions.cost: unknown vendor cost; (a) costs 0 but starts the clock at zero observations
questions.verified_by: absence is verifiable: the committed extract has no open-line or timestamp column, checked in audit_root.py

questions.question: Is the league's injury policy text obtainable?
questions.known: The URL the root site cites (operations.nfl.com/football-ops/league-governance/injury-report/) returns 404 on 2026-11-12. The live injury report page itself works and is the data source this project uses.
questions.unknown: The current edition of the policy. Secondary reporting describes a three-part report (practice, game status, in-game) with Wednesday-Thursday-Friday filings and a 90-minute inactive list, but that is not an official text and is not relied on.
questions.how_to_answer: Ask the league for the current Personnel (Injury) Report Policy, or find it on an NFL-operated domain. Until then, treat the reporting rules as described-but-unverified and do not build a rule on them.
questions.cost: 1 hour to check, unbounded to obtain
questions.verified_by: 404 confirmed on 2026-11-12; the live report page confirmed in the same session

questions.question: Which settlement rulebook governs every backtest?
questions.known: The repository cites a DraftKings Massachusetts filing (8.1.24) that the regulator lists as obsolete; the active edition is the one approved 10.7.26. Push handling, void legs and minimum leg counts differ by operator.
questions.unknown: Which operator, and therefore which rulebook, is the standard. Also unknown: whether the 10.7.26 PDF text matches the old edition on the rules that matter (it could not be fetched in the sandbox).
questions.how_to_answer: A reviewer decision: pick one operator's filed rules as the standard, record the edition, and re-price the backtest if it changes.
questions.cost: 1 hour to decide, 2 days to re-price
questions.verified_by: the regulator's own archive and licensee pages were read; the edition change is documented

questions.question: Is the reward pool real?
questions.known: No. The reward tiers are a design proposal. No money, sponsor, eligibility rules or payout mechanism exists.
questions.unknown: Whether there will be money, and if so its source, tax treatment and eligibility.
questions.verified_by: the absence is stated on the root flagged page and in the leaderboard data

questions.question: Which of the nine sibling dashboards is canonical?
questions.known: The root site is canonical and generated by scripts/build_site.py; eight sibling directories are preserved but outside the navigation. Several of them contradict the root's numbers because they were built from different data windows.
questions.unknown: Whether the reviewer wants them archived (S-13), kept reachable, or deleted.
questions.how_to_answer: A reviewer decision; nothing is deleted either way.

questions.question: Is the '2026 Week 10' injury report the same week the model thinks it is?
questions.known: Yes for this snapshot: nfl.com/injuries/ renders 'WEEK 10', and the tracker's league_week is 10 with 24 of 32 teams on week 10 and 8 teams on week 9 (they have not filed a week-10 report or are on bye).
questions.unknown: Nothing material. The earlier sessions hit a page whose title said week 8 while the body said week 7; that discrepancy does not reproduce on 2026-11-12.
questions.how_to_answer: Already answered; the tracker publishes latest_week_by_team so the mismatch is visible per team rather than pooled.
questions.verified_by: rendered page read 2026-11-12 and compared with the derived JSON

questions.question: Do the published correlations reproduce from a clean checkout?
questions.known: Partly. The signs and magnitudes reproduce; the sample size does not (7,560 published vs 6,024 recomputed) because the committed extract covers 2015-2026 while the published coefficients used 2012-2026. The project records this as 'DIFFERS (expected)'.
questions.unknown: Whether any conclusion changes at the smaller n. The joint-vs-product gap holds within tolerance (11.14% vs 10.94%, 5.69% vs 5.55%).
questions.how_to_answer: Re-run the analysis on the committed extract and republish the n, or commit the extract the coefficients were measured on.

questions.question: Can a prop ROI ever be measured with the data here?
questions.known: No. The feed has player box scores but no historical prop prices. Prop accuracy and calibration can be measured; ROI cannot.
questions.unknown: Whether a historical prop-price source exists that this project can license.
questions.how_to_answer: Same acquisition problem as Q-05. Until then, publish calibration and Brier skill only, and leave ROI blank.
questions.verified_by: absence is verifiable in the committed extract columns

questions.question: Is the gate screen itself working?
questions.known: Untested. Two controls exist and both fail, so the screen has never been shown to pass anything. A screen that cannot pass a bettor who knows the result is not evidence about real candidates.
questions.unknown: Whether the gates are mis-wired. The clairvoyant positive control has not been run.
questions.how_to_answer: Add a clairvoyant control (bet the actual winner at the stored price) and require it to pass. If it fails, fix the gates before reading any verdict.
questions.verified_by: data/derived/leaderboard.json: both control entries are REJECTED

questions.question: Does the depth-chart rank agree with who actually played?
questions.known: Not yet tested. The tracker assigns a rank from the depth chart and a snap share from the snap counts, but the two have not been compared.
questions.unknown: How often the '2nd string' player on the chart is the one who takes the snaps. If it is often wrong, the whole deficiency measure is noise.
questions.how_to_answer: For each position, correlate chart rank with snap share the following week. Publish the agreement rate per position. Only then is a rank-based feature defensible.
questions.verified_by: the data to answer it is now committed (ranks and snap shares are on every absence row)

questions.question: What is the actual cost of the acquisition steps?
questions.known: Nothing. No vendor quotes, no licence terms, no API tiers were obtained.
questions.unknown: Whether the project can afford the data it needs to answer Q-05, Q-06 and Q-12.
questions.how_to_answer: Get written quotes from at least two licensed odds vendors and one official data distributor; record the terms of use. A reviewer decision on budget.
questions.cost: 3 hours to request, unknown to buy
questions.verified_by: the NFL's official data distributor arrangement is documented; pricing is not public

questions.question: Which numbers on the site are official facts rather than our computations?
questions.known: The site already classifies sources into 'league official', 'regulator', 'sportsbook official', 'academic' and 'community', but the numbers themselves are not labelled by class on the page.
questions.unknown: Nothing structural. The classification exists; only the per-row label is missing.
questions.how_to_answer: Add a 'class' column to every table row, generated from the source register rather than typed. This is suggestion S-01.
questions.verified_by: data/sources.json carries a 'type' on all 58 entries
